items.stem: A muon travelling near light speed is observed to live far longer than its rest-frame lifetime. This is explained by

options.text: time dilation: moving clocks run slow in the lab frame
options.rationale: Correct: special relativity predicts time dilation for fast-moving particles.

options.text: the muon gaining mass and becoming stable
options.rationale: Increased relativistic energy does not make the muon stable.
Muon decay is not a chemical process.
The effect is a real, repeatable relativistic prediction.

items.stem: Why does nuclear fusion of light nuclei release energy?

options.text: The product nucleus has a higher binding energy per nucleon, so mass is converted to energy
options.rationale: Correct: moving toward the binding-energy peak releases energy via E = mc^2.

options.text: Light nuclei are radioactive and decay

options.rationale: Energy is conserved; it comes from the mass defect.

options.text: The nuclei are pushed apart by the strong force
options.rationale: The strong force binds nucleons together.
